questions.q: The principle of design that uses the repetition of elements (such as lines, shapes, or colours) to direct the viewer's eye across the artwork and create a feeling of motion is known as:
questions.explain: Rhythm (often associated with movement) is created by repeating elements in a pattern or sequence, creating a visual tempo or beat that guides the viewer's eye through the artwork.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: In textile design, when a specific geometric motif is stamped repeatedly at regular intervals across a fabric, which principle is predominantly at work?
questions.explain: Repetition of a single motif at regular intervals creates a pattern, which is the foundational basis for visual rhythm in a design, commonly seen in textiles.
